metadata.method: Asset-level subagent research packets. Overrides are applied after CT.gov and openFDA ingestion.
metadata.coverage_note: Tildrakizumab records have completed source-backed packets. All other assets retain generated provenance plus pending research assignments until their own subagent packet is added.

NCT06488170.mechanism: Humanized IgG1/k monoclonal antibody that selectively binds the IL-23 p19 subunit and blocks IL-23 receptor interaction.
NCT06488170.clinical_summary: Post-approval real-world wellbeing study in plaque psoriasis. Tildrakizumab is an established adult plaque-psoriasis biologic dosed 100 mg SC at Weeks 0 and 4, then every 12 weeks; key label risks include hypersensitivity, infections, TB screening, and avoiding live vaccines.
evidence_gaps: No posted ClinicalTrials.gov results for NCT06488170 as of 2026-05-27
Real-world QoL study does not represent a new-product launch
Net payer cost depends on rebates, buy-and-bill economics, and site-of-care controls

expected_launch_window.method: FDA approval / marketed-status override plus CT.gov trial classification
expected_launch_window.explanation: ILUMYA is already FDA-approved and marketed for adult plaque psoriasis; the CT.gov record is a post-approval real-world study and should not be treated as initial launch timing.

annual_cost_range.method: Drug-specific WAC disclosure annualized to labeled dosing
annual_cost_range.explanation: Sun Pharma's WAC disclosure lists $16,416.64 per 100 mg syringe. The range approximates maintenance-year to first 52-week/loading-year dosing under the label and excludes rebates, administration, wastage, and site-of-care effects.

clinical_differentiation.explanation: NCT06488170 is a prospective observational real-world wellbeing study, not an interventional label-enabling trial. It may inform QoL evidence but is unlikely to materially change formulary positioning by itself.

budget_impact.method: Drug-specific WAC plus post-approval evidence context
budget_impact.explanation: The product is already on market and the study is observational, so incremental budget impact is lower than for a launch or label expansion; total budget impact remains sensitive to net cost and utilization management.

disruption_risk.explanation: Risk is medium because ILUMYA is a high-cost biologic with payer controls, but NCT06488170 is post-approval QoL evidence rather than a new launch or label-expansion trigger.

recommended_action.method: Mapped from marketed status and trial purpose
recommended_action.explanation: Monitor real-world QoL results and payer-policy implications; do not initiate new-product launch planning for this record.

NCT06611163.mechanism: Humanized IgG1/k monoclonal antibody that selectively binds the IL-23 p19 subunit and blocks IL-23 receptor interaction.
NCT06611163.clinical_summary: Phase 3 randomized, double-blind, placebo-controlled genital psoriasis study; if positive, it could support a high-impact site-specific label or payer-policy expansion.
evidence_gaps: No posted ClinicalTrials.gov results for NCT06611163 as of 2026-05-27
No current FDA genital psoriasis indication identified in the 2025 label
Limited head-to-head evidence versus preferred IL-23/IL-17 agents in genital psoriasis
Net payer cost depends on rebates, buy-and-bill economics, and site-of-care controls

sources.title: A Study to Evaluate the Efficacy and Safety of Tildrakizumab in Subjects With Genital Psoriasis
Sun Pharma Connecticut WAC disclosure for ILUMYA
Aetna clinical policy bulletin for tildrakizumab-asmn

expected_launch_window.method: FDA approval / marketed-status override plus CT.gov label-expansion classification
expected_launch_window.explanation: ILUMYA is already FDA-approved and marketed; NCT06611163 is a Phase 3 genital psoriasis study and should be tracked as a potential label or policy expansion, not initial launch.

annual_cost_range.method: Drug-specific WAC disclosure annualized to labeled dosing
annual_cost_range.explanation: Sun Pharma's WAC disclosure lists $16,416.64 per 100 mg syringe. The range approximates maintenance-year to first 52-week/loading-year dosing under the label and excludes rebates, administration, wastage, and site-of-care effects.

clinical_differentiation.explanation: The trial is Phase 3, randomized, double-blind, and placebo-controlled in moderate-to-severe genital psoriasis. A positive result could support a high-impact site-specific label or payer-policy expansion.

budget_impact.explanation: Genital/groin involvement can be treated as a high-impact site even with lower BSA. A label or policy expansion could increase eligible utilization for an already high-cost biologic.

disruption_risk.explanation: Risk is high because a near-term Phase 3 label-expansion signal could affect PA criteria and preferred biologic positioning for a high-impact psoriasis subpopulation.

recommended_action.explanation: Prepare label-watch, evidence-review, and policy-scenario materials for genital psoriasis; do not treat the product as a new-product launch.

NCT03997786.mechanism: Humanized IgG1/k monoclonal antibody that selectively binds the IL-23 p19 subunit and blocks IL-23 receptor interaction.
NCT03997786.clinical_summary: Phase 2/3 pediatric plaque-psoriasis study in ages 6 to under 18 with placebo and etanercept comparator components plus long-term extension; could support pediatric label monitoring while longer-term evidence matures.
evidence_gaps: No posted ClinicalTrials.gov results for NCT03997786 as of 2026-05-27
No current FDA pediatric indication identified in the 2025 label
Long-term pediatric extension evidence remains immature
Net payer cost depends on rebates, buy-and-bill economics, and site-of-care controls
